name: Reputation

verdict.line: Enterprise horizontal ORM that names multifamily as a vertical and integrates with Yardi, Entrata and RealPage — expect it on large-portfolio shortlists, and compete on what happens after the reply, not on feature count.

ownership.value: Private; significant growth investment from Marlin Equity Partners

pricing.value: Not published. A pricing page is linked but shows no tiers or costs.

positioning.value: Self-described as "The #1 AI-Powered Reputation Management Software," turning reviews, listings and surveys into actionable intelligence for multi-location brands.

strengths.text: Multifamily / property management is a named industry vertical with a dedicated real-estate solution page.
Lifecycle review requests (renewal, post-maintenance) triggered from PMS integrations with Yardi, Entrata and RealPage.
Competitive Insights tracks nearby-community ratings, themes and response times; Portfolio Benchmarking flags outlier properties.
Corporate → regional → property permission model with pre-approved templates and approval workflows for fair-housing-sensitive language.
Reputation IQ supports plain-language questions across resident data; Rep Score rolls signals into one KPI.

gaps.text: No training, policy management or mystery-shopping capability — the platform is reviews, listings, social, surveys and analytics.
No pricing is published; the pricing link resolves to a contact path rather than tiers.
Real-estate is one of eight named verticals alongside automotive, healthcare, food & beverage, senior living, retail and financial services — multifamily is not the primary market.

whyWeWin: Grace Hill's reputation data lives beside training completion, policy attestation, survey scores and shop results, so a regional can see whether the fix actually happened.
Fair housing is not a template setting for us — it is the same content library the onsite team is trained and tested on.
A multifamily-only roadmap means resident-lifecycle changes land in the product without competing against seven other verticals for priority.
askThis: Which of your review responses are drafted by AI and approved by whom — and what is your audit trail if a fair housing complaint cites a public reply?
Reputation names eight industries. Which of the last four releases changed something specific to apartments?
Their deployment is quoted at 30–45 days. What does your team have to do during that window, and who does it?
Once Competitive Insights tells you a comp out-responds you, what is the operational change on site?

objections.objection: Reputation is the enterprise standard; our owners know the name.
objections.response: Fair. Ask what the platform does with a finding. Grace Hill's answer is an assignment to a person with a due date and a completion record — that is the part an owner can audit.

objections.objection: They integrate with our PMS already.
objections.response: So do we, and integration is table stakes now. The differentiator is whether the reputation signal reaches the person who can fix it.

doNotSay: Do not repeat or dispute their '#1 AI-powered' marketing claim on a call — it is unfalsifiable and drags the conversation onto their turf.
Do not say they 'don't do multifamily' — they publish a real-estate vertical page with named PMS integrations.

rm-monitoring.note: Review monitoring across properties with corporate oversight.

rm-response-managed.note: Real-estate page describes both managed response and on-site team responses under corporate oversight; scope of the managed offering is not detailed publicly.

rm-response-ai.note: AI-assisted response with pre-approved templates and approval workflows.

rm-generation.note: Automated SMS/email review requests triggered at lease renewal and post-maintenance via PMS integration.

rm-gbp.note: Listings and local SEO work covers Google surfaces, maps and 'near me' discovery.

rm-listings.note: Property details, photos and amenities optimized across listing platforms.

rm-social.note: Social publishing and response with corporate control and visibility.

rm-analytics.note: Rep Score by building and region; Reputation IQ natural-language querying across resident data.

rm-competitor-bench.note: Competitive Insights tracks nearby-community ratings, themes and response times.

rm-property-rollup.note: Corporate → regional → property hierarchy with portfolio benchmarking and outlier flags.

name: Birdeye

verdict.line: Broad horizontal reviews-and-listings platform with a real property-management page and named PMS integrations; the multifamily buyer gets tooling and AI drafting, not a multifamily response team.

pricing.value: Not published. Pricing page is a form gated on number of locations (1-3 through 1000+). States "Pricing built around outcomes, not seat counts."

positioning.value: Reviews, listings, social and insights for property management, integrated with the systems operators already run.

strengths.text: Monitoring and review generation across 200+ sites, with requests sent by text or email.
Named PMS integrations: Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, Rent Manager, AppFolio, Follow Up Boss.
Modular AI product set — Reviews AI, Listings AI, Social AI, Insights AI — in a single platform and contract.
States 3,400+ properties and communities on the platform.

gaps.text: No managed / done-for-you review response service is described on the property management page or the pricing page; responses are AI-drafted or written by the client's team.
Pricing is not published — the pricing page is a lead form requiring location count and contact details.
No training, policy management, mystery shopping or multifamily benchmark index in the product set.

whyWeWin: Grace Hill's reputation line is built for multifamily roles and fair housing obligations, and it sits beside the training and policy records that prove the operator acted.
A recurring review theme in PerformanceHQ can become a course assignment or a shop — Birdeye ends at the dashboard.
Our benchmarks come from a multifamily dataset, not a cross-industry local-business dataset.
askThis: Who writes your review responses today — onsite staff, corporate marketing, or a vendor's team?
If an AI-drafted reply used language a fair housing tester flags, what is your review and approval trail?
Which of the sites your prospects actually use — ApartmentRatings, Apartments.com, Zillow — does the platform post responses to, not just read from?
Once a review theme is identified across a region, who gets assigned what, and how do you show it was completed?

objections.objection: Birdeye is cheaper per location.
objections.response: Ask what the per-location price includes and who does the responding. If your onsite teams write the replies, the real cost is their hours and your fair housing exposure, not the license.

objections.objection: They integrate with everything.
objections.response: Integration breadth is a horizontal platform's job. Ask which of the integrations trigger a multifamily-specific workflow versus just syncing a location record.

doNotSay: Do not say Birdeye 'can't do multifamily' — they publish named PMS integrations, a property management page and case studies.
Avoid 'the only platform that…' framing here; Birdeye's feature list is broad and a prospect can disprove a superlative in one search.

rm-response-managed.note: No managed response service is described on the property management or pricing pages.

rm-response-ai.note: "Use AI to generate tailored, error-free responses with a single click."

rm-generation.note: Automated review requests by text or email across 200+ sites.

rm-gbp.note: Listings AI manages Google and other directory profiles.

rm-listings.note: Listings AI creates, updates and manages listings across hundreds of directories.

rm-social.note: Social AI creates and publishes posts across multiple locations from one dashboard.

rm-analytics.note: Insights AI provides sentiment measurement and analysis.

rm-competitor-bench.note: Benchmarking against competitors is described on the property management page; multifamily-specific comp-set construction is not detailed.

rm-property-rollup.note: Portfolio-wide management across many locations from a central dashboard.

name: SOCi

verdict.line: Local-marketing platform reframed as AI agents, with a real property-management vertical and named multifamily logos — it wins the marketing conversation, so move the conversation to operations.

funding.value: $120M round led by JMI Equity; earlier $80M Series D also led by JMI (Jan 2021)

positioning.value: An "agentic AI workforce" of Genius Agents for Local Search, Reputation and Social, deployed across every location of a multi-location brand.

strengths.text: Property Management is one of six named industry verticals with a dedicated solution page.
Names multifamily operators as customers including Willow Bridge, Bridge Property Management, SunRidge Management Group and Anchor Pacifica; states 5,000 properties on the platform.
Reputation agent responds across Google, Zillow, Caring.com and Apartments.com with either full automation or an approval workflow.
Covers paid social (Ads & Boost) and SEO local pages, which pure ORM vendors do not.

gaps.text: Review generation / solicitation is not described on the property management solution page.
No managed human review-response service is described; responses come from a trained AI agent with optional approval workflow.
No pricing is published on the site.

whyWeWin: SOCi is bought by marketing; PerformanceHQ is bought by operations and marketing together, which is where the resident-experience budget actually sits.

Fair housing language review in our workflow is grounded in the same compliance content library the onsite team is trained on.
askThis: If the reputation agent auto-publishes a reply, who at your company is accountable for the fair housing language in it?
How does a review-driven insight get from marketing to the regional who owns the property?

How are you generating new reviews today — is that inside SOCi or a separate tool?

objections.objection: SOCi already handles our social and listings, adding reviews is trivial.
objections.response: Consolidating publishing makes sense. Ask a different question: when reviews say the maintenance response time is the problem, does anything happen outside marketing?

objections.objection: Their AI agents respond automatically at scale.

doNotSay: Do not claim SOCi has no multifamily customers — they publish named operator logos.

name: Opiniion

verdict.line: Multifamily resident-feedback platform whose center of gravity is review generation and automation, sold at published entry pricing — it shows up as the cheap line item, not as the reputation program.

pricing.value: Published entry points: three tiers (Build, Connect, Scale), each with a $99/month minimum, plus a one-time $249 per-property setup fee. Full per-property pricing is quoted after a demo.

positioning.value: AI-powered resident feedback platform that aggregates reviews, surveys, maintenance requests and leasing notes into one dashboard for multifamily, student housing and senior living.

strengths.text: Publishes entry pricing — $99/month tier minimums and a $249 per-property setup fee — which few vendors in this category do.
Property teams control which review sites residents are directed to and at what distribution weight.
Can run "fully automatically — collecting feedback, generating reviews, sending reports, and even responding to reviews via AI."
Covers student housing and senior living alongside conventional multifamily.

gaps.text: No managed human review-response service is described; responses are AI-generated or team-written.
The FAQ does not name specific PMS integration partners, deferring to a separate integrations page.
Competitor benchmarking is not described on the homepage or FAQ.
No training, policy management or mystery-shopping line.

whyWeWin: Grace Hill's survey program is benchmarked against a multifamily dataset, so a score has a comparison set behind it rather than only an internal trend.
Reputation in PerformanceHQ connects to training, policy and shopping data, so the operator can act on a theme instead of only observing it.
Governance matters at portfolio scale — role-based approval on public replies is part of the platform, not an option to switch on.
askThis: If review responses can post fully automatically, who approves the language before it goes live on a fair-housing-sensitive complaint?
How are you steering which residents get asked for a review, and does that survive an owner's scrutiny?
What do you compare your scores against — your own history, or a comp set?
At $99 minimums per tier plus $249 per property, what does the real number look like at your unit count?

objections.objection: Opiniion is a fraction of the price.
objections.response: It is priced as a feedback tool, and that is what it is. Compare it against the whole job — benchmarked surveys, response governance, and the training and policy follow-through that changes the score.

objections.objection: We just need more reviews.
objections.response: Volume moves the average for a quarter. Ask what happens to the underlying complaint themes; that is what keeps the average up.

doNotSay: Do not suggest their review solicitation is review gating or non-compliant — there is no public source and the claim carries legal risk.
Do not quote a total price; the published figures are minimums and a setup fee, not a full quote.

name: Entrata ReputationAdvisor

verdict.line: A reputation module inside the PMS your buyer already pays for — it wins on procurement friction, so compete on managed response, benchmarking and what happens after the reply.

founded.value: 2003 (18 years bootstrapped as of the 2021 raise)

funding.value: $507M round led by Silver Lake with Ryan Smith and Todd Pedersen (announced July 2021)

positioning.value: A reputation module inside the Entrata platform that aggregates reviews and uses Entrata Layered Intelligence (ELI) to generate responses in one click.

strengths.text: Aggregates reviews from Yelp, Google, ApartmentRatings.com "and other sites" with updates within 24 hours.
ELI generates review responses with a single click, inside the system onsite teams already work in.
Multi-property reporting with portfolio-wide trend analysis and per-property performance.
Social publishing with scheduling and permission controls is part of the module.
No new vendor, no new login, no separate integration project.

gaps.text: Review generation / solicitation is not described on the ReputationAdvisor product page.
Google Business Profile management and listings management are not described on the product page.
Competitor benchmarking is not described on the product page.
No managed human response service is described; responses are AI-drafted or team-written.
Pricing is not published.

whyWeWin: A PMS module reports on the properties inside that PMS; operators running mixed PMS estates get one reputation view from Grace Hill across all of them.
PerformanceHQ links a reputation theme to a training assignment, a policy acknowledgment and a shop result, and keeps the completion record.
Benchmarking against a multifamily comp set is part of what we sell, not something the operator has to assemble.
askThis: Do all your properties run on Entrata, or do you have acquisitions on another PMS?
If you leave Entrata, what happens to your reputation history and your response archive?
Who is generating new reviews today — is that inside ReputationAdvisor or a separate tool you also pay for?
How do you know whether your response times beat the comps in your submarket?
When a review theme is consistent across a region, what training or policy step is triggered, and where is that recorded?

objections.objection: It's already included in what we pay Entrata.
objections.response: Then use it for monitoring. The gap is generation, benchmarking and follow-through — price those separately and see whether the bundled module actually covers them.

objections.objection: We don't want another login.
objections.response: Reasonable. Note that most operators end up with a separate tool for review generation and listings anyway; the question is how many logins you end up with either way.

doNotSay: Do not state that Entrata 'cannot' do listings or benchmarking — say it is not described on their public product page and confirm with the prospect.
Avoid superlatives about cross-PMS coverage; describe the specific portfolio scenario instead.

rm-monitoring.note: Yelp, Google, ApartmentRatings.com and other sites, updated within 24 hours.

rm-response-managed.note: Not described on the product page.

rm-response-ai.note: Entrata Layered Intelligence (ELI) generates responses with a single click.

rm-generation.note: Not described on the product page.

rm-gbp.note: Google reviews are aggregated; GBP profile management is not described.

rm-listings.note: Not described on the product page.

rm-social.note: Scheduling and planning posts across social platforms with permission controls.

Avoid dismissing them by size on a call; state the specific capability gaps and let the prospect draw the conclusion.

whenItComesUp.why: Overlaps in part, not in whole. Early-stage multifamily AI marketing startup with a reputation module — watch it, do not build a battlecard motion around it yet.
whenItComesUp.say: Concede the part they genuinely own, then be specific about the part they don't. Partial overlap is where reps over-claim and lose credibility.
whenItComesUp.avoid: Do not characterize MavenAI as unstable or unfunded — no public funding or financial data was located.
whenItComesUp.redirect: Who reviews AI-published responses before they go live on a fair-housing-sensitive complaint?

spiced.listenFor: They name Maven AI, hiremaven.ai, Maven Reputation Management, or describe multifamily-specific orm already in place.
spiced.ask: Who reviews AI-published responses before they go live on a fair-housing-sensitive complaint?

spiced.listenFor: Competitor benchmarking is not described on the reputation management product page.

spiced.listenFor: Whether the gap costs them money, time or exposure — or is just an annoyance.
spiced.ask: If that stayed exactly as it is for another year, what does it cost you?

spiced.listenFor: A renewal date on the MavenAI contract, an audit, an acquisition, or new leadership asking what the data shows.
